stem: A company planned to sell 10,000 units in a quarter but actually sold 7,500 units. Its manager says the size of the shortfall will decide what corrective action is needed. Which statement best evaluates the link between planning and controlling here?
options: Controlling is independent of planning, since sales are measured directly
The plan gave the standard; the 25% deviation guides the corrective action
Planning failed, because the plan did not guarantee the target would be met
The deviation shows that standards should be set after measuring results
explanation: Correct option: (B). The planned 10,000 units is the standard. Shortfall = 10,000 - 7,500 = 2,500 units, i.e. 2,500/10,000 = 25%. The nature of corrective action depends on the extent of deviation from the standard, so planning provides the basis of control. Controlling is not independent of planning, a shortfall does not mean planning was useless (planning never guarantees success), and standards must be set in advance, not after measuring results.
